The definition of validation for machine learning (ML) models differs from that for medical devices (MD) in that ML validation is primarily focused on algorithm tuning and unbiased evaluation of model performance, specifically regarding the selection of hyperparameters to avoid overfitting. In contrast, validation for medical devices encompasses a broader scope, aiming to demonstrate clinical benefit, achievement of intended use, and appropriate safety and performance of the entire device.

The role of clinical evaluation in the context of medical devices is crucial, as it is part of the validation process that confirms the safety, performance, and clinical benefit of the product. This evaluation includes scientific validity, analytical performance, and clinical performance, ensuring that the device meets the specified goals for its intended use.
